stories.headline: Update: Supreme Court Opens New Term With Cases on Climate Liability, Gun Rights, and Immigration
stories.summary:
The U.S. Supreme Court began its new term Monday with a packed docket that includes a major climate liability case, gun rights disputes, immigration policy challenges, and religious liberty questions. Among the first items, the court turned away a gun industry challenge to a New York law that allows lawsuits against firearms manufacturers, wholesalers, and dealers for endangering public safety through their sales practices.

The term's marquee case involves whether federal law preempts state and local government lawsuits seeking billions of dollars in climate damages from major oil companies. Dozens of such cases have been filed by governments facing mounting costs they attribute directly to fossil fuel emissions. The court's ruling could determine the fate of climate liability litigation nationwide.

The new term also places the justices in tension with the Trump administration, which has lost several major cases in recent months while openly criticizing individual justices. The court is expected to take up Trump's immigration policies, giving the administration another opportunity to prevail on issues central to its agenda.

Conservative justices are also facing scrutiny after Justice Samuel Alito said in a CBS News preview that his vote to overturn Roe v. Wade in Dobbs required 'courage.' The comment is likely to intensify ongoing political debate over the court's legitimacy and direction heading into the midterm election season.

stories.headline: Update: FlyDubai Co-Pilot Used Crash Axe in Attack on Captain, UAE Prosecutor Confirms
stories.summary:
The United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has confirmed that the co-pilot of a FlyDubai flight to Tel Aviv attacked the aircraft's captain with a crash axe in an attempt to seize control of the plane. The flight, carrying more than 170 passengers, plunged approximately 17,000 feet before passengers overpowered the attacker and allowed injured Captain Smit Machchhar to regain enough control to open the cockpit door. Two reserve pilots then safely landed the aircraft in Saudi Arabia.

The attacker has been identified as an Omani national. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, speaking to Fox News, said the co-pilot cried out 'Kill me, kill me!' after being subdued, and called it 'clear that he was suicidal.' Netanyahu said the attacker appeared to have 'undergone Islamist radical indoctrination.' The UAE has launched an investigation into whether the incident was linked to terrorist activity.

Captain Machchhar, who sustained stab wounds, has been airlifted to Abu Dhabi and is reported to be in stable condition. The Indian embassy confirmed he is 'in good health and recovering well.' Passengers described a terrifying plunge resembling a rollercoaster before they rushed the cockpit. An Israeli woman onboard was credited with raising the alarm after hearing a commotion from the flight deck.

This update represents a significant escalation in the confirmed details of the attack, moving from earlier reports of a stabbing to the UAE's official confirmation of an axe attack and the opening of a formal terrorism investigation.

stories.headline: Update: French Student Protests Escalate Further; 1,747 Arrested as Violence Spreads Nationwide
stories.summary:
Riot police clashed with demonstrators across France on Friday as student protests over education conditions escalated sharply into widespread civil unrest. Interior Minister Laurent Núñez announced 1,747 arrests, and the protests have now disrupted more than 700 of France's 3,700 schools. Fires were set in streets in Paris, Rennes, and other cities, and police deployed tear gas in Strasbourg.

The protests began last week in Paris over grievances including a shortage of teachers, overcrowded classrooms, and deteriorating school facilities. French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said the movement had transitioned from student demonstrations into 'a public order disturbance,' while Education Minister Édouard Geffray said non-students had hijacked the movement. A 17-year-old was arrested in Belfort on suspicion of attempted homicide after a police officer was beaten, with authenticated video showing the officer punched and kicked in the head. At least 65 staff members have been injured.

Students maintain their demands are legitimate and accuse police of heavy-handed tactics. 'It makes us even angrier — the police have no right to hit us or use tear gas on us,' said one 16-year-old protester. Nelson Mandela High School in Nantes suffered more than €2 million in damage after fire destroyed its entrance.

The updated arrest total of 1,747 — a dramatic rise from previously reported figures — marks a material escalation from prior coverage and signals the crisis is deepening rather than stabilizing, putting significant pressure on the French government ahead of expected further protests.

stories.headline: Car Plows Into Crowd of Australian Rugby Fans, Injuring 10 Including Young Children
stories.summary:
A vehicle drove into a crowd of spectators north of Sydney on Saturday morning as fans gathered to send off the Newcastle Knights rugby team ahead of a league finals match. Ten people were injured, including several children. A 5-year-old girl and a 67-year-old man were in critical condition; among those in stable condition were two other girls aged 5 and 2.

New South Wales police arrested the 18-year-old male driver at the scene. Authorities stated the crash was not believed to be related to terrorism and that an investigation into the circumstances was underway. Thousands of fans had been gathering throughout the week to support the Knights as they prepared for their finals appearance.

The incident occurred on a public road where large numbers of supporters had congregated to watch the team bus depart. The Rugby League finals are among the most-watched sporting events in Australia, drawing significant crowds to team events across the country.

No motive has been publicly confirmed. Police have not released the driver's name or indicated whether charges beyond arrest have been filed.
